prompt: The provided Describable interface has default methods describe() and shout(), where shout() builds on describe(). Complete Robot: implement kind() and override the default describe(), then watch shout() pick up your override.
explanation: Default methods give an interface reusable behavior, but a class is always free to override them just like any inherited method. shout() calls describe() on 'this', so once Robot overrides describe(), shout() automatically uses the overridden version -- dynamic dispatch applies to default methods too. Implementors that do not override describe() (like the lambda in the tests) keep the interface's default.
hints: Override describe() in Robot with the public modifier, and build its text by calling kind() instead of hard-coding the word.
Do not override shout() -- it already calls describe(), and at runtime that resolves to your override.
